Training in bf16 halves memory traffic, but a small weight update can vanish
completely. This post works out exactly when.

## How a bf16 number is stored

A bf16 number has 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 7 mantissa bits:

$$
x = (-1)^s \times 1.m \times 2^{e - 127}
$$

With 7 mantissa bits, the gap between neighbouring numbers near $x$ is

$$
\text{gap}(x) = 2^{\lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor - 7}.
$$

Near $x = 1$ the gap is $2^{-7} \approx 0.0078$.

## When an update disappears

Round-to-nearest drops any update smaller than half the gap. So the update
$w \leftarrow w - \eta g$ is lost whenever

$$
|\eta g| < \tfrac{1}{2}\,\text{gap}(w) = 2^{\lfloor \log_2 |w| \rfloor - 8}.
$$

For $w = 1$, learning rate $\eta = 10^{-3}$ and gradient $g = 1$, the update is
$10^{-3}$, below half the gap ($\approx 0.0039$), so the weight never moves.

```python
import torch
w = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
print(w - 1e-3)   # tensor(1., dtype=torch.bfloat16): the update vanished
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## The fix
Keep an fp32 master copy of the weights and apply updates there. fp32 has 23
mantissa bits, so its gap near 1 is $2^{-23} \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-7}$.
:::
